hypotheses.reasoning: GET /search collapsed at ~01:16. At 01:15:00 search-api reloaded config revision 747, which changed CATALOG_SVC_URL to http://catalog-svc.internal:8081 (#1793). Starting at 01:16:03 every search-api call to catalog-svc fails with connection refused, dialing 10.23.138.197:8081 (#1875, #1905, #1978), and search-api then returns errors upward. web-bff reports GET /search 503 from search-api (#1920, #2046), which is the symptom at the edge. catalog-svc logs no errors and keeps serving with normal GC pauses, so the target service is not crashing; search-api is pointed at a dead or wrong endpoint. The one-minute drop in /search success matches the reload timing. Before the reload, search-api and catalog-svc were healthy (#1798, #1799 200 OK). Other errors in the window are unrelated to /search: auth-svc S3 PutObject 500/503 (#1549, #1714, #1911) causing /login failures, and status-poller timeouts against deprecated legacy-inventory (#1812). Those are red herrings for this alert.

Lower-ranked: AWS S3 us-east-1 returning 500/503 for auth-svc PutObject. This explains /login 500s and account-svc token failures, but not /search, since search-api does not call S3 and the failure is on the catalog-svc connection path. Ruled out as the cause of this alert.

verdict.recommendedAction: Revert search-api CATALOG_SVC_URL to the previous value (roll back config-service revision 747 or correct the endpoint), then reload or restart search-api so it dials the live catalog-svc. Confirm that 10.23.138.197:8081 is the wrong address and that catalog-svc.internal resolves to the healthy instance. Verify /search success recovers. Separately, follow up on the auth-svc S3 PutObject failures, which affect login only.
